Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
FromCSDepartment(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJobOfferedByUniversity(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x takes the database course.
InstructedByProfessorD(x) ::: x is instructed by professor David.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
HasPartTimeJobOfferedByUniversity(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
Question:
James is a student working in the lab. Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Premises:
∀x (¬(Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x))) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x ((PartTimeJobOfferedByUniversity(x) ∧ Student(x)) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university work in the library.
∀x (TakesDatabaseCourse(x) → FromCSDepartment(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (InstructedByProfessorD(x) → TakesDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → InstructedByProfessorD(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
Student(James) ∧ WorksInLab(James) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(PartTimeJobOfferedByUniversity(Jack) ∧ WorksInLab(Jack)) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Conclusion:
James ∨ PartTimeJobOfferedByUniversity(James) ::: James either takes the database course or has a part-time job offered by the university.
